### 1. **Ask First — And Ask Often**
Before critiquing or commenting on someone, ask if they're comfortable hearing it. Then, keep asking.

> *"Do you mind if I say something about her outfit? I just saw her and thought it was interesting."*  
> *"Would you be okay if I say something about the way he’s been dressing lately?"*  
> *"Would you mind if I gave you my take on her hair choice?"*

When you do speak, be precise. Don’t generalize. And when you can, offer kindness in your critique.

> *"I like the way she styled her hair — it’s so different from what I’ve seen her do before."*  
> *"I noticed the way he wore that blazer; it looked like it was borrowed or maybe a little too big."*  
> *"Her makeup was really bold tonight — I thought it was brave."*

Avoiding words like *ugly*, *fat*, *disgusting*, or *weird* doesn’t mean you can’t have an opinion. Just speak your opinion *as if someone might hear it*.

> *"Her hair was so different tonight, but I love the way she did her eyes."*

- Encourage realistic and achievable standards.
